_readme: HAWAIʻI HOLIDAY CALENDAR -- 2026, thirteen dates, derived from HRS Sec. 8-1
and checked by weekday.
THE REFERENT IS EXPRESS, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT IDAHO'S WAS NOT. Haw. R. Civ.
P. 6(a) ends: 'As used in these rules, "holiday" shall mean any day
designated as such pursuant to SECTION 8-1 of the Hawaiʻi Revised Statutes.'
One section, named by number. No chain to trace and no competing list.
FOUR OF THE THIRTEEN EXIST ON NO OTHER CALENDAR IN THIS PLATFORM: Prince
Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole Day (26 March), King Kamehameha I Day (11 June),
Statehood Day (third Friday in August), and GOOD FRIDAY -- Hawaiʻi is the
only seeded state to make Good Friday a legal holiday, and the provision
survived an Establishment Clause challenge (932 F.2d 765). Good Friday is
DERIVED from the computus, not transcribed.
AND THREE THAT ITS NEIGHBOURS HAVE AND HAWAIʻI DOES NOT: no Juneteenth, no
Columbus or Indigenous Peoples' Day, no day after Thanksgiving. A calendar
copied from Nebraska would add three days Hawaiʻi does not have and miss
four it does.
*** THE SEC. 8-2 WEEKEND SHIFT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED. *** HRS Sec.
8-2 observes a Saturday holiday on the preceding Friday and a Sunday holiday
on the following Monday. But Rule 6(a) incorporates SECTION 8-1 BY NUMBER,
and a Sec. 8-2 day is designated pursuant to Sec. 8-2. Idaho and Nebraska
both carry their shifts because there the shift clause sits in the SAME
section the rule points at; Hawaiʻi's does not. Omitting reports EARLY;
carrying would report LATE. IN 2026 THIS AFFECTS EXACTLY ONE DATE -- 4 July
is a Saturday, so Sec. 8-2 would make FRIDAY 3 JULY 2026 an observed holiday
and this calendar does not carry it. A practitioner will treat that Friday
as a court holiday; check any date in that week by hand.
THE GENERAL ELECTION DAY IS ALSO OMITTED. Sec. 8-1 designates 'all election
days, except primary and special election days, IN THE COUNTY WHEREIN THE
ELECTION IS HELD' -- county-scoped by its own words, and needing a second
statute to fix the date. Neither was resolved on a primary source, so it is
omitted rather than computed.
2026 ONLY. Twelve of the thirteen would generate mechanically and Good
Friday from the computus, which is precisely why a later year is refused:
generating would hide the Sec. 8-2, election-day and proclamation questions
behind a confident answer.

authority.citation: Haw. R. Civ. P. 6(a) via HRS Sec. 8-1
authority.quote: Sec. 8-1 Holidays designated. The following days of each year are set apart and established as state holidays: The first day in January, New Year's Day; The third Monday in January, Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Day; The third Monday in February, Presidents' Day; The twenty-sixth day in March, Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole Day; The Friday preceding Easter Sunday, Good Friday; The last Monday in May, Memorial Day; The eleventh day in June, King Kamehameha I Day; The fourth day in July, Independence Day; The third Friday in August, Statehood Day; The first Monday in September, Labor Day; The eleventh day in November, Veterans' Day; The fourth Thursday in November, Thanksgiving Day; The twenty-fifth day in December, Christmas Day; All election days, except primary and special election days, in the county wherein the election is held; Any day designated by proclamation by the President of the United States or by the governor as a holiday.
authority.note: ONE SECTION, NAMED BY NUMBER. Haw. R. Civ. P. 6(a) closes with 'As used in these rules, "holiday" shall mean any day designated as such pursuant to section 8-1 of the Hawaiʻi Revised Statutes' -- an express referent, and the contrast with Idaho seeded the day before is exact: there the rule said 'legal holiday' and stopped, and the statute, the Secretary of State's page and the courts' own closures disagreed three ways. FOUR DATES HERE APPEAR ON NO OTHER CALENDAR IN THIS PLATFORM: Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole Day, King Kamehameha I Day, Statehood Day, and Good Friday. GOOD FRIDAY IS THE ONLY COMPUTED-FROM-EASTER DATE IN THE WHOLE ENGINE: Sec. 8-1 says 'the Friday preceding Easter Sunday', so it is derived from the computus rather than read off a schedule -- Easter 2026 is 5 April, so Good Friday is 3 April. It is also the only religious observance any seeded state makes a legal holiday, and the statute's own case note records that it survived an Establishment Clause challenge, 932 F.2d 765. STATEHOOD DAY IS A FLOATING DATE (third Friday in August) and Prince Kuhio Day and King Kamehameha Day are fixed; all three are Hawaiʻi-only and a copied calendar misses every one. THREE THINGS THE NEIGHBOURS HAVE AND HAWAIʻI DOES NOT: Juneteenth, Columbus/Indigenous Peoples' Day, and the day after Thanksgiving. Nebraska enumerates all three. THE SEC. 8-2 WEEKEND SHIFT IS NOT CARRIED, AND THAT IS A READING. HRS Sec. 8-2 observes a Saturday holiday on the preceding Friday and a Sunday holiday on the following Monday, but Rule 6(a) incorporates SECTION 8-1 by number and a Sec. 8-2 day is designated pursuant to Sec. 8-2. Idaho's Sec. 73-108 and Nebraska's Sec. 25-2221 each contain their own shift clause, which is why those two are carried and this one is not. Omitting reports EARLY, carrying would report LATE. IN 2026 IT AFFECTS EXACTLY ONE DATE: 4 July is a Saturday, so Friday 3 July 2026 would be the observed holiday and is absent here. No other Sec. 8-1 holiday falls on a weekend in 2026. 4 JULY ITSELF IS CARRIED, faithfully, and being a Saturday it is excluded by the weekend limb regardless. THE ELECTION-DAY LIMB IS OMITTED: 'all election days, except primary and special election days, IN THE COUNTY WHEREIN THE ELECTION IS HELD' is county-scoped by its own words and needs a second statute to fix the date; neither was resolved on a primary source, so it is omitted rather than computed. THE PROCLAMATION LIMB IS OMITTED for the usual reason. All three omissions run EARLY. 2026 ONLY: a later year is REFUSED rather than derived.

dates.name: New Year's Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the first day in January'. 1 January 2026 is a Thursday.

dates.name: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the third Monday in January', computed for 2026 and verified by weekday.

dates.name: Presidents' Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the third Monday in February', computed for 2026 and verified by weekday.

dates.name: Prince Jonah Kuhio Kalanianaole Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the twenty-sixth day in March'. 26 March 2026 is a Thursday. HAWAIʻI-ONLY: no other calendar in this platform has this date, and it commemorates the Prince who served as Hawaiʻi's delegate to Congress.

dates.name: Good Friday
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the Friday preceding Easter Sunday'. DERIVED FROM THE COMPUTUS, the only such date in this engine: Easter 2026 falls on Sunday 5 April, so Good Friday is 3 April, verified as a Friday. Hawaiʻi is the ONLY seeded state to make Good Friday a legal holiday; the statute's own case note records that the provision survived an Establishment Clause challenge, 932 F.2d 765.

dates.name: Memorial Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the last Monday in May', computed for 2026 and verified by weekday.

dates.name: King Kamehameha I Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the eleventh day in June'. 11 June 2026 is a Thursday. HAWAIʻI-ONLY.

dates.name: Independence Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the fourth day in July'. 4 JULY 2026 IS A SATURDAY. HRS Sec. 8-2 would observe it on Friday 3 July, and that Friday is DELIBERATELY NOT in this calendar -- Rule 6(a) incorporates Sec. 8-1 by number and the shifted day is designated pursuant to Sec. 8-2. See the authority note. The Saturday itself is carried faithfully and is excluded by the weekend limb regardless, so this entry changes no computation.

dates.name: Statehood Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the third Friday in August', computed for 2026 and verified as a Friday. HAWAIʻI-ONLY, and a FLOATING date -- a hardcoded value is wrong every year.

dates.name: Labor Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the first Monday in September', computed for 2026 and verified by weekday.

dates.name: Veterans' Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the eleventh day in November'. 11 November 2026 is a Wednesday.

dates.name: Thanksgiving Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the fourth Thursday in November', computed for 2026 and verified by weekday. THE DAY AFTER IS NOT A HAWAIʻI HOLIDAY and is deliberately absent -- Nebraska enumerates it, Hawaiʻi does not.

dates.name: Christmas Day
dates.derivation: HRS Sec. 8-1, 'the twenty-fifth day in December'. 25 December 2026 is a Friday.
